newsitem.title: USA: Argentina, Brazil upgrade not warranted - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Argentina, Brazil upgrade not warranted - Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday that the default risks of Argentina and Brazil had not declined enough to warrant an upgrade.
"We don't see that their (Argentina/Brazil) default risks have declined enough to warrant an upgrade," said Kristin Lindow a sovereign analyst with Moody's Investors Service.
Moody's currently rates Argentina and Brazil's long-term foreign currency debt at B1 with a stable outlook.
Earlier today, Standard & Poor's, another major U.S. credit rating agency raised Argentina's $62.2 billion of long-term foreign currency debt to BB from BB-minus.
In addition, S&P upgraded Brazil's $54.1 billion of long-term foreign currency debt, including Brady Bonds, to BB-minus from B-plus.

"If we moved the ratings up to a Ba3 level that would suggest that we would reduce, by several percentage points, our estimation of the risks. We just don't feel that that kind of reduction in risks has taken place as yet," Lindow told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"From our perspective, we feel the ratings are at the appropriate level for both countries."
